claims.statement: For every finite bipartite H, subset W, integer a with alpha(H)<=a-1, and integer k>=1, if q_j counts independent j-subsets of H meeting W with zero extension, then k*q_(k+1)<=2(a-1-k)*q_k; consequently for a tree leaf term at p=alpha(T)-2 and alpha(T)>=7, Delta_(p-1)(H)-Delta_(p-1)(R)<=0.
claims.scope: Informal combinatorial proof of the tagged deletion/extension count and its stated leaf-derived specialization; no selector, residual, connectivity, or nonempty-family assumption is needed for the count.
claims.reason: Double count gives at least k witness-preserving deletions per tagged upper set and at most 2(alpha(H)-k) available extensions per tagged lower set; all zero/empty cases are handled without division.

claims.statement: Every ordinary finite connected tree T with p=alpha(T)-2 and first strict descent x(T) satisfying x(T)+2<=p has alpha(T)>=7.
claims.scope: Informal exact proof by eligibility guards, exact Delta_0/Delta_1/Delta_2 identities, and n=7/n=8 vertex-cover boundary cases.
claims.reason: Each alpha=4,5,6 possibility contradicts the required first strict descent; in the alpha=6 case Delta_2 is nonnegative for n>=9 and positive in the exact n=7,8 cases.

limitations: No Lean build, formal fidelity audit, or primary-gate verification was assigned or run; all mathematical claims are proposed informal results and registry status remains unchanged.
The independent DP replay covers the constructive examples m=4,5,11 only; no exhaustive ordinary-tree search was run or needed for the general proof.
